# Gallium

> Gallium is a browser skill for AI agents with a local engine. Use it in place of the default browser skill and hand it a goal through MCP or the CLI. One request can cover a direct read or several steps in Chrome. Gallium returns a source passage or checks the result of a configured change.

## Start here

- [Use cases](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/#use-cases): Check a product before buying, fill a form, and change a setting in a signed-in app.
- [Demos](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/#workflow): Route diagrams for catalog, pickup, profile, and host browser fallback tasks.
- [Benchmarks](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/docs/benchmarks.html): Measured medians, verified fixture outcomes, and reproduction commands.
- [Engine architecture](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/#engine): Route selection, live feedback, durable state, concurrency, and human handoff.
- [Quickstart](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/#install): Install, configure, and run the first lookup from the homepage.
- [Agent setup prompt](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/#agent-prompt): One prompt to install the engine and skill, configure the router, and try a public lookup.
- [Agent setup instructions](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/setup.txt): Plain-text instructions referenced by the one-line prompt.
- [Agent skill](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/#install-skill): Run `npx skills add davidjbeveridge/gallium` in your agent project. Use the local CLI or MCP server and add “Use the Gallium skill for web tasks.” to the project's agent instructions.
- [Documentation](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/docs/): All project guides and reference pages.
- [Setup and configuration](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/docs/guide.html): Configure the CLI, stdio MCP server, Chrome bridge, model router, and procedures.
- [Validation](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/docs/validation.html): Test commands, observed outcomes, and qualification boundaries.

## How the engine works

- Public goals use a configured Jev router through OpenRouter System One. Gallium tries direct HTTPS for document lookups and can move to bounded, same-origin browser exploration. Explicit UI goals start in the live page. The result includes a source URL, passage, and evidence hash. The model assesses relevance.
- Configured goals match existing procedures. Code prefers direct HTTP, then browser-session requests, then browser interaction among eligible web procedures. Signed-in workflows and mutations require a configured account, allowed actions, and an independent result check. The browser routes use installed desktop Chrome through the bridge.
- Gallium chooses its next browser action from the current page. Configured route preference is fixed. The SQLite journal keeps the operation ID, chosen procedure, effects, and human ownership across restarts.
